messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — 7 nodes in prod-east-1 showing repeated 'CUDA illegal memory access' events; affected pods: serving-runtime-v3 (replicas across three node pools). Automated rollback to cpu-variant attempted for 2 pods. Severity: P1.
ops-oncall: seeing same. pod restarts spiking ~1m intervals. cpu/mem on nodes look fine, but dmesg shows 'invalid device address' traces. starting triage.
maria-eng: can someone grab a stack trace and nvml logs from a crashed container? suspect kernel/gpu driver race during pagewalk.
kevin-sre: grabbing logs now. command I ran: `kubectl -n prod logs -p serving-runtime-v3-7fbk2 --container=runtime` — getting `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` at token generation loop. also capturing `dmesg` and `kubectl describe node` outputs.
kevin-sre: dmesg snippet: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00:0: RMA: Illegal memory access at 0x7f... offset 0x1f4`
ops-oncall: tagging infra-bot to check recent kernel/driver rollouts: @infra-bot any deploys last 24h to prod-east-1?
infra-bot: deployment-log: kernel-5.15.0-rc1 (host image) rolled to nodepool-gpu-a 6h ago; nvidia-driver 535.54.03 updated 5h ago. No config changes to kubelet.
maria-eng: ok that narrows scope. 535 driver + kernel combo might be the regression. can we cordon nodepool-gpu-a and drift traffic while we repro?
ops-oncall: cordoning nodepool-gpu-a now. `kubectl cordon node gpu-a-03 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-a-03` will migrate pods, but expect restarts on other pools.
ryan-support: customer-impact: A few high-throughput customers (acct-psi, acct-green) report increased 5xxs and timeouts over last 20m. reaching out to account-advocate for proactive comms.
account-advocate: notified teams for acct-psi and acct-green; drafting advisory: short blip causing generation failures, mitigation in progress; ETA 30m for full stabilization.
kevin-sre: while cordon is running, attaching GDB to a crashing container to capture backtrace; using `gdb --pid` inside debug image. saving `/tmp/crash-backtrace.txt`.
maria-eng: upload backtrace to thread when done. also capture `nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses` around crash time if possible.
kevin-sre: uploaded: `/tmp/crash-backtrace.txt` includes repeated frames in `request_loop()` -> `kv_cache_load()` -> `device_memmap_walk()` — looks like pagewalk edge-case.
ops-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) cordon/drain nodes with new kernel/driver, 2) temporarily scale up dedicated pool on kernel-stable nodes, 3) if crashes persist, fail traffic to cpu-variant (via routing policy) for affected customers. executing steps 1/2 now.
maria-eng: agree. also preparing an immediate runtime patch to gate the new memory-mapping optimization (optimize_sparse_mmaps=false) and push a canary to a single replica on stable nodes.
ops-oncall: scale-up done: added 8 instances to nodepool-gpu-b (kernel-stable). new replicas spun up and traffic shifted. crash rate dropped by ~80% in last 6m.
ryan-support: acct-psi reported partial recovery after 5m, but still seeing occasional failed inferences for large-context requests. customer requested ETA for root cause.
account-advocate: sent update: we mitigated major impact by shifting traffic; engineering is investigating root cause (possible kernel/driver interaction). will provide RCA in follow-up.
kevin-sre: repro attempt on a stable node with canary binary that disables sparse mmaps — so far no repro after 30 runs with heavy paging. attaching logs: `canary-run-30.log`.
maria-eng: good sign. next steps: 1) prepare rollout of runtime toggle (optimize_sparse_mmaps=false) across clusters as temporary mitigation, 2) coordinate with infra to rollback driver 535 -> 530 on a small pool for reproduction matrix, 3) open bug with driver vendor with backtrace and repro.
ops-oncall: creating incident ticket in tracker: INC-2026-3452. Adding timeline and comms.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3452 created by ops-oncall. Severity=P1. Slack thread linked.
ryan-support: handoff note for next oncall: all urgent mitigations applied (drain of gpu-a nodes, traffic shifted to stable nodepool, runtime toggle canary running). Remaining work: vendor bug, targeted rollback test, full rollout of runtime toggle if vendor fix delayed.
ops-oncall: tagging next oncall @kevin-sre for 19:00 UTC handoff. please monitor crash rate and customer tickets; escalate to ENG if >10% error rate persists.
kevin-sre: acked. will continue monitoring and follow up with scheduled updates every 30m.
account-advocate: final note to customers: mitigation in place, limited residual errors for large-context workloads; will notify when full rollback/fix is planned. :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: thanks team — keeping thread open for follow-ups, will add RCA link once vendor response and our reproduction matrix are complete.
